yes.title: Touch-shot ally
yes.t: Turns and ==carries straight at low power== for slow arms.

yes.title: No-flick solution
yes.t: Gives ==forehand-style lines off a backhand== for players without one.

no.title: Big arms overpower it
no.t: Flat or ripped throws ==turn straight into a roller==.

no.title: Finicky control
no.t: Short shots and forehands ==need careful touch==; hyzer flips can go too far.

no.title: Niche bag slot
no.t: Rarely ==earns an everyday spot==, despite doing shots nothing else does.

kastaplast-berg.tagline: A zero-glide approach disc that stops near the pin. The catch: it needs a hard throw to go anywhere.
kastaplast-berg.bottom: A distance-control approach disc for beginners and intermediates. Skip it as a long-range putter.

yes.title: Distance control
yes.t: Runs out of air and ==drops without skipping past==.

yes.title: Angle control
yes.t: Takes power ==without turning over==, holding the release line.

yes.title: Sidearm favourite
yes.t: Concave top ==locks in for soft forehand approaches==.

no.title: No glide
no.t: It ==demands a hard throw== to reach even short targets.

no.title: Tricky to putt
no.t: Can ==be hard to sink== from beyond close range.

no.title: Changes with wear
no.t: K3 and old K1 Soft ==lose late stability== as they beat in.

streamline-pilot.tagline: A glidey, straight throwing putter. The catch: plastic choice swings it from stable to flippy.
streamline-pilot.bottom: A point-and-shoot putter for beginners and intermediates. Skip it if you need one stable plastic.

yes.title: Point-and-shoot control
yes.t: Flies ==dead straight with a gentle late fade== on approaches.

yes.title: Easy reach
yes.t: Glide ==carries it as far as most midranges== with little effort.

yes.title: Hand feel
yes.t: Flat top and micro-bead ==sit naturally for forehands and backhands==.

no.title: Run lottery
no.t: Plastic choice ==swings it from overstable to flippy==; Eclipse splits opinion.

no.title: Durability concerns
no.t: Baseline Electron can ==chunk or warp==; worn copies lose stability.

no.title: Flips if forced
no.t: Yanked throws can ==turn and burn==, like a flippier Proxy.

axiom-proxy.tagline: A dead-straight, beadless throwing putter. The catch: stability varies by run and plastic.
axiom-proxy.bottom: A go-to straight putter for beginners and intermediates. Skip it if you want a reliable fade.

yes.title: Point-and-shoot accuracy
yes.t: Holds ==any release angle to the ground== with almost no fade.

yes.title: Hand feel
yes.t: Beadless, low rim ==releases cleanly with a tacky grip==.

yes.title: Two-in-one utility
yes.t: Putts true ==with spin or push== and still drives well.

no.title: Batch lottery
no.t: Stability ==varies by run and plastic==, from Envy-stable to flippy glow.

no.title: Escapes when ripped
no.t: Snapped or flat full-power throws can ==turn over==; it's no hyzer disc.

kastaplast-jarn.tagline: An overstable approach putter with a hard dump. The catch: K1 and K3 fly like different discs.
kastaplast-jarn.bottom: A utility approach disc for intermediate and advanced players. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Torque-proof finish
yes.t: Fights out of forced anhyzers and ==dumps hard on every throw==.

yes.title: Forehand favourite
yes.t: Handles ==hard sidearm flicks and flex shots== cleanly.

yes.title: Hand feel
yes.t: K1 and K1 Soft ==grip well and absorb landings==.

no.title: Plastic swings
no.t: K1 and K3 ==fly like different discs==; K3 is shorter with little glide.

no.title: Unusual shape
no.t: Splits opinion: the deep rim and dome ==take time to get used to==.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Little glide and ==a hard dump== suit players who already control approaches.

prodigy-pa-5.tagline: A shallow, understable throwing putter for turnovers. The catch: fast flat throws nearly roll.
prodigy-pa-5.bottom: Great for woods turnovers and newer arms. Skip it if you want a stable putter.

yes.title: Shot-shaping putter
yes.t: Flips up and ==holds slow right-turning lines== through woods.

yes.title: Pleasant in hand
yes.t: Shallow, rounded lip ==feels comfortable and grippy==.

yes.title: Beginner friendly
yes.t: Easy flip-ups and ==floating glide== suit newer and slower arms.

no.title: Hard to rip
no.t: Flat, fast throws ==turn it nearly into a roller==.

no.title: Specialty slot
no.t: Can be ==a niche disc== used only a couple of times a round.

no.title: Plastic changes it
no.t: 750 runs ==fly beefy==, while 300 drifts right the most.

mvp-uplink.tagline: A very understable midrange for hyzer flips and turnovers. The catch: flat releases turn over fast.
mvp-uplink.bottom: Great for newer players and anyone without a forehand. Skip it if you want a late fade.

yes.title: Right-moving tool
yes.t: Carves ==long, smooth turnovers without burning out==, a fix for no forehand.

yes.title: Clean flip-ups
yes.t: Stands up from a hyzer and ==flies straight through tight woods==.

yes.title: Easy for slower arms
yes.t: Moderate power gets ==260-270 ft without effort==, even with rough form.

no.title: Little margin
no.t: Flat, torqued or headwind releases ==turn over fast and can burn out==.

no.title: Plastic shifts it
no.t: Glow and lab runs ==fly a tick more stable==; a 169 g copy turns over easier.

no.title: Hand feel
no.t: Splits opinion: the ==thin, soft rim== suits some grips and not others.

innova-fox.tagline: A glidey, understable midrange for flip-ups and turnovers. The catch: power turns it hard right.
innova-fox.bottom: Great for newer players and wooded hyzer flips. Big arms wanting a straight mid should skip it.

yes.title: Effortless flip-ups
yes.t: Stands up off a hyzer and ==drifts right on a long, floaty line==.

yes.title: Huge glide
yes.t: Carries ==further than most mids with little effort==, past 300 ft.

yes.title: New-player friendly
yes.t: Gives ==easy, forgiving distance== to beginners, even with a rough release.

no.title: Flips with power
no.t: Torque or 55+ mph arm speed ==turns it hard right==, worst in Star and GStar.

no.title: Varies by run
no.t: Halo, Champion, Duo and 180 g copies ==hold more and fight back== than light Star.

dynamic-discs-justice.tagline: A beefy overstable utility midrange for wind and flex shots. The catch: little glide, so it flies short.
dynamic-discs-justice.bottom: Built for intermediate and advanced players needing wind and utility shots. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Wind-proof utility
yes.t: Shrugs off ==howling headwinds on approaches and upshots==.

yes.title: Forehand workhorse
yes.t: Handles ==hard flex lines and full torque without flipping==.

yes.title: Predictable finish
yes.t: Ends with ==a reliable skip or a hard spike== on cue.

no.title: Little glide
no.t: It ==starts fading almost out of the hand== and flies short.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Takes ==real effort and anhyzer to reach a 200 ft pin==, too beefy for many.

discraft-sol.tagline: A shallow, very understable midrange for flip-ups and turnovers. The catch: full power rolls it.
discraft-sol.bottom: Great for slower arms and wooded flip-up lines. Strong arms wanting a straight mid should skip it.

yes.title: Easy flip-ups
yes.t: Stands up from a hyzer and ==rides flat with tons of glide==.

yes.title: Turnover tool
yes.t: Holds ==long right-drifting anhyzer lines without fading back==.

yes.title: Low-power friendly
yes.t: Gentle throws ==get easy distance==, ideal for newer and slower arms.

no.title: Burns for big arms
no.t: Full power ==turns it over into a roller==, even off hyzer.

no.title: Tricky on tight lines
no.t: Can ==drift further right than planned==, too squirrelly for narrow tunnels.

westside-anvil.tagline: A beefy, beadless overstable approach midrange. The catch: little glide, so it dumps hard and early.
westside-anvil.bottom: Built for intermediate and advanced players needing wind and flex approaches. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Headwind approaches
yes.t: Ignores ==strong wind on upshots and short tee shots==.

yes.title: Torque-proof utility
yes.t: Takes ==full-power anhyzers and hard forehands, then flexes back==.

yes.title: Corner skipper
yes.t: Ends ==with a hard dump and big skip== around sharp doglegs.

no.title: Little glide
no.t: It ==dumps hard and early==, so it suits set utility shots only.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Moderate arms get ==a hard left dump with no easy distance==.

no.title: Plastic-dependent landings
no.t: Ground play ==varies by blend==: Origio skips around, BT Soft sits down.

discraft-zone-os.tagline: A brick-stiff overstable approach putter. The catch: too beefy for straight touch shots.
discraft-zone-os.bottom: Built for intermediate and advanced players' forehand flex and wind shots. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Won't flip
yes.t: Takes ==max power and forced anhyzers with zero turn==.

yes.title: Flex-shot specialist
yes.t: Wraps ==high forehand lines around trees==, 50-200 ft out.

yes.title: Wind anchor
yes.t: Fades and gets down ==reliably in howling crosswinds==.

no.title: Too beefy for touch
no.t: Very little glide ==makes straight approaches hard to judge==.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: It ==hooks left almost out of the hand==, even in baseline Jawbreaker.

no.title: Backhand comfort
no.t: The deep, flat rim ==feels clunky in a fan grip==.

dynamic-discs-deputy.tagline: A shallow, understable putter for straight putts and turnovers. The catch: power or headwinds flip it.
dynamic-discs-deputy.bottom: Great for newer players and touch turnover shots. Skip it if you putt into headwinds a lot.

yes.title: Easy straight lines
yes.t: Pops up off a hyzer and ==flies true without hyzering out early==.

yes.title: Gentle turnovers
yes.t: Flat or anhyzer releases ==drift right without fighting back==.

yes.title: Comfort in hand
yes.t: A ==shallow, beadless profile== that putts glidey from 15 to 50 ft.

no.title: Easy to overpower
no.t: Too much juice or a headwind ==can flip it and dump it right==.

no.title: Plastic matters
no.t: Firm Classic ==flies a touch straighter== than Prime or Classic Blend.

no.title: Durability gap
no.t: Classic Blend ==chunks up fast near trees and rocks==; Classic lasts longer.

mvp-tesla.tagline: A stable 9-speed control driver for forehands. The catch: fresh copies fly beefier than rated.
mvp-tesla.bottom: For intermediate and advanced arms wanting a reliable fade. Beginners and slower arms should skip it.

yes.title: Dependable control
yes.t: A 9-speed workhorse that ==holds flat and fades on cue==.

yes.title: Forehand friendly
yes.t: A flat, shallow top ==sits well in a sidearm grip== and takes power.

yes.title: Steady in wind
yes.t: Stays flat ==into headwinds and breezy days==.

no.title: Beefier than rated
no.t: New copies ==fly far more overstable than -1/2==, closer to a Firebird.

no.title: Plastic and weight
no.t: Light Fission ==flies straightest==; heavy Neutron and Fission hook earlier.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Needs ==11-12-speed effort to fly as rated==; slower arms get a hook.

innova-valkyrie.tagline: A classic understable 9-speed for easy distance. The catch: DX and worn copies turn into rollers.
innova-valkyrie.bottom: Great for slower arms and newer players chasing distance. Big arms wanting a lasting fade should skip it.

yes.title: Easy hyzer flips
yes.t: Stands up and ==carries downfield with a gentle turn==, no big arm needed.

yes.title: Long carry
yes.t: Matches ==the range of most distance drivers==, 330-370 ft for solid arms.

yes.title: Shapeable both ways
yes.t: Carves ==S-curves off forehand and backhand== around obstacles.

no.title: Beats in flippy
no.t: DX and worn copies ==turn into rollers within months==.

no.title: Stability lottery
no.t: Champion, glow and max-weight Star runs ==fly far more overstable==.

no.title: Touchy when ripped
no.t: Can ==flip over easily==, rolling on full-power forehands.

latitude-64-fuse.tagline: A glidey, understable midrange for flip-ups and turnovers. The catch: it can turn over unexpectedly.
latitude-64-fuse.bottom: Great for beginners and wooded turnover lines. Big arms wanting a reliable fade should skip it.

yes.title: Effortless flip-ups
yes.t: Stands up gently from a hyzer and ==pushes straight with endless glide==.

yes.title: Turnover lines
yes.t: Holds ==smooth right-drifting anhyzers without burning in==.

yes.title: Beginner pick
yes.t: Needs ==minimal power for straight distance== as a starter mid.

no.title: Flippy and erratic
no.t: Can ==turn over and roll== on a throw that flew straight before.

no.title: Changes with use
no.t: Retro and Opto ==beat in to more turn==; Gold Ice holds longer.

innova-leopard.tagline: An understable 6-speed fairway driver for turnovers and control. The catch: stability swings by plastic.
innova-leopard.bottom: Great for slower arms and wooded turnover shots. Big arms needing a lasting fade should skip it.

yes.title: Turnover tool
yes.t: Holds ==right-turning anhyzers and hyzer flips== on wooded holes.

yes.title: Easy to control
yes.t: Slower arms get it ==up to speed for neutral, predictable lines==.

yes.title: Long for a 6-speed
yes.t: Flipped right, it ==reaches distance-driver range==, about 340 ft.

no.title: Plastic swings it
no.t: Champion and Star ==fly far more stable than DX or Pro==, which flip early.

no.title: Overpowered easily
no.t: Full power, light 146 g copies and forehands ==turn it over and can roll it==.

no.title: Dents easily
no.t: Light DX ==bends and changes flight after tree hits==.

mvp-resistor.tagline: A flat, overstable 6.5-speed for forehands and fades. The catch: runs range from beefy to straight.
mvp-resistor.bottom: Built for intermediate and advanced forehand and utility throwers. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Forehand weapon
yes.t: A flat top and thin rim ==take full-power sidearms without turning==.

yes.title: Reliable hook
yes.t: Pushes briefly, then ==finishes with a sharp, dependable fade==.

yes.title: Wind fighter
yes.t: Holds up ==in brisk headwinds with brute stability==.

no.title: Run lottery
no.t: Runs ==range from Firebird beef to Teebird straight==; Eclipse is stiffest.

no.title: Beats in
no.t: Neutron copies ==can wear into a flippy flight==, some almost overnight.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Takes ==practice to dial in==, and it is very overstable early on.

innova-aviar.tagline: A classic beadless, straight-flying putter. The catch: the deep rim feels bulky in a lot of hands.
innova-aviar.bottom: A great first putter for newer players wanting straight lines. Skip it if you like a shallow putter.

yes.title: Benchmark putter
yes.t: Flies ==dead straight and holds the line you give it==.

yes.title: Floaty touch
yes.t: Carries ==a long way on approaches==, easing right when worn.

yes.title: Grippy plastics
yes.t: Star, XT and DX ==give a tacky, sure hold==.

no.title: Divisive fit
no.t: The ==deep rim feels bulky or loose== in a lot of hands.

no.title: Base plastic wears
no.t: DX ==beats in quickly and turns over==; tree hits change its flight.

no.title: Lifts and floats
no.t: Can ==glide long and drift in wind==, so a stabler putter suits gusty days.

axiom-insanity.tagline: An understable 9-speed for easy, straight flip-up distance. The catch: stability swings by plastic.
axiom-insanity.bottom: Great for moderate arms wanting straight distance. Skip it if you need every copy to fly the same.

yes.title: Easy flip-ups
yes.t: Stands up from a hyzer and ==holds long, straight lines==.

yes.title: Versatile 9-speed
yes.t: Works ==backhand and forehand on woods lines and touch shots==.

yes.title: Flex lines
yes.t: Holds an anhyzer ==for most of the flight before a soft fade==.

no.title: Stability by plastic
no.t: Eclipse, glow and Plasma ==fly far more overstable==; Fission and Proton turn.

no.title: Keeps getting flippier
no.t: Fission ==beats in to a turnover machine==; Neutron and Eclipse settle.

no.title: Erratic at times
no.t: Can ==fly unpredictably==: light copies wander, the slim rim slips when wet.

innova-roc3.tagline: A beaded, overstable midrange with a sure fade. The catch: copies vary from hooking to near straight.
innova-roc3.bottom: Great for players wanting one mid for fades and wind. Skip it if you dislike beaded rims.

yes.title: Dependable fade
yes.t: Holds flat, then ==finishes with a predictable late hook==.

yes.title: Cycleable mold
yes.t: Plastics and wear ==cover overstable, straight and turnover slots==.

yes.title: Built for wind
yes.t: Fresh Champion and Metal Flake ==fight headwinds with zero flip==.

no.title: Run differences
no.t: Copies vary: new Champion ==hooks hard==, some Star and Luster fly near straight.

no.title: Loses its bite
no.t: DX and McPro ==wear in fast== and stop fading out of an anhyzer.

no.title: Divisive bead
no.t: Splits opinion: the rim ==never sits right== in some hands.

kastaplast-reko.tagline: A straight, low-glide putter that putts and drives. The catch: its grip shifts in cold, wet and heat.
kastaplast-reko.bottom: A great straight putter and driver for beginners. Skip it if you often play in cold or wet weather.

yes.title: True flight
yes.t: Throws ==dead straight off the tee and into the chains==.

yes.title: Grippy blend
yes.t: K3 ==sits between firm and tacky==, releasing clean without sticking.

yes.title: Calm in breezes
yes.t: Moderate glide keeps it ==reliable when the wind picks up==.

no.title: Weather swings grip
no.t: Feel changes: ==slick in cold or damp, gummy or sticky in heat==.

no.title: Putting fit
no.t: Splits opinion: the ==flat, low feel doesn't suit every stroke==.

no.title: Base plastic wears
no.t: K3 ==beats in quickly== and needs cycling often.

mvp-volt.tagline: A flat, stable 8-speed fairway driver for forehands. The catch: new runs hook like a Firebird.
mvp-volt.bottom: For intermediate and advanced arms wanting fade and wind control. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Reliable placement
yes.t: Pushes ==straight before a dependable forward fade==.

yes.title: Wind fighter
yes.t: Holds ==flat through brisk headwinds==.

yes.title: Forehand friendly
yes.t: The flat top ==makes clean, powerful sidearm throws==.

no.title: Overstable surprise
no.t: New Neutron, Cosmic and Plasma ==hook like a Firebird==, beefier than rated.

no.title: Soft blends wear
no.t: Electron ==can get flippy or bend== after weeks of tree hits.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Moderate arms get ==a hard dump and short carry==, about 300 ft max.

mvp-atom.tagline: A straight, shallow beadless putter for putts and approaches. The catch: the rim feel splits opinion.
mvp-atom.bottom: Great for beginners wanting a point-and-shoot putter. Skip it if you prefer a deep, beaded rim.

yes.title: Point-and-shoot putter
yes.t: Holds ==a dead-straight line on short shots and approaches==.

yes.title: Low-profile feel
yes.t: A ==shallow, beadless rim releases cleanly== off the fingers.

yes.title: Surprising reach
yes.t: Thrown nose down, it ==carries 300 ft and beyond== off the tee.

no.title: Divisive fit
no.t: Splits opinion: the rim ==feels awkward or hard to spin== in some hands.

no.title: Wind can move it
no.t: Its glide ==can let gusts push it off line==.

no.title: Soft blend wear
no.t: Electron ==beats up fast==; Neutron and Proton last longer.

innova-pig.tagline: A low-glide, overstable approach midrange that drops on target. The catch: R-Pro loses its fade fast.
innova-pig.bottom: Built for intermediate and advanced players' approaches inside 250 ft. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Approach precision
yes.t: Drops ==fast and sits down near the pin== without skipping away.

yes.title: Chunky grip
yes.t: The thick rim and thumb track ==give a sure, confident hold==.

yes.title: Torque-resistant flight
yes.t: Fights out of ==heavy anhyzer on backhand and forehand==.

no.title: Beats in fast
no.t: R-Pro and GStar ==lose their fade within months== and fly straighter.

no.title: Polarizing rim
no.t: Splits opinion: the ==deep thumb track feels awkward== in some hands.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Fresh copies are ==absurdly overstable== and need anhyzer to fly true.

innova-roc.tagline: A classic beaded midrange that seasons from fade to turnover. The catch: every copy flies differently.
innova-roc.bottom: Great for newer players and anyone who cycles a mold. Forehand-first players should skip it.

yes.title: Cycles beautifully
yes.t: Fresh copies fade, then ==season into straight and turnover flights==.

yes.title: Dependable control
yes.t: Holds ==a straight line before a gradual, predictable fade==.

yes.title: Great teacher
yes.t: Neutral and easy to fly level, it ==builds a clean release==.

no.title: Run-to-run swings
no.t: Batch and wear ==make every copy fly differently==; DX wears fastest.

no.title: Polarizing feel
no.t: The tall bead ==is hard to adjust to==, worst on forehands and in Champion.

no.title: Prone to wobble
no.t: Can ==flutter off-axis== when torqued.

latitude-64-ballista-pro.tagline: A 14-speed overstable bomber for big arms. The catch: Opto-X and Opto Air runs fly very differently.
latitude-64-ballista-pro.bottom: Built for power arms, flex lines and headwinds. Beginners and slower arms should skip it.

yes.title: Big-arm distance
yes.t: Reaches ==about 400 to 450 ft== on flex lines and forehands.

yes.title: Power-proof flight
yes.t: Takes full speed ==without turning and burning==, then fades predictably.

yes.title: Headwind tool
yes.t: ==Stays on line into nasty wind== with a dependable left finish.

no.title: Plastic and run swings
no.t: Opto-X and Chameleon fly ==much beefier== than Opto or Gold; Air can flip.

no.title: Seasoned copies change
no.t: Years of wear ==turn it flippy enough to hyzer flip==.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Needs ==serious arm speed== to unlock its full flight.

innova-sonic.tagline: A floaty, understable utility putter for touch shots. The catch: it can flip with power or wind.
innova-sonic.bottom: A great touch and escape disc for any level. Skip it if you play in steady wind.

yes.title: Floaty touch shots
yes.t: Glides ==a long way on slow, nose-up releases== without needing power.

yes.title: Escape-shot specialist
yes.t: Holds ==slow right-turning anhyzers== around trees with little power.

yes.title: Close-in utility
yes.t: Covers ==approaches, jump-putt range and trick shots== with touch.

no.title: Pushed off line
no.t: Can ==flip with extra power==, and headwinds make angle control hard.

no.title: Brittle base plastic
no.t: DX copies ==can crack or shatter== after tree hits; Star lasts longer.

no.title: Odd in the hand
no.t: The lid shape ==feels awkward at first== and can keep it from main-putter duty.

streamline-echo.tagline: A straight, glidey midrange that holds its line. The catch: it ends with only a baby fade.
streamline-echo.bottom: Ideal for beginners and intermediates wanting a straight mid. Skip it if you need a hard finish.

yes.title: Laser accuracy
yes.t: Holds ==whatever line it's put on==, from tunnel shots to gentle turnovers.

yes.title: Easy carry
yes.t: High glide ==pushes it farther down the fairway== without a big arm.

yes.title: Bendy premium option
yes.t: Proton Soft runs ==feel grippy== in hand and cuts down ground play.

no.title: Little finish
no.t: Ends ==with only a mild fade==, so wind can push Neutron runs off line.

no.title: Blend and wear shifts
no.t: OTB Soft and beat-in copies ==turn a little more== than stock runs.

innova-yeti-aviar.tagline: A deep, beaded puddle-top putter that flies straight. The catch: the Pro plastic gets gummy in heat.
innova-yeti-aviar.bottom: A grippy, straight putter for beginners and bead fans. Skip it if you play in hot summers.

yes.title: Signature hand feel
yes.t: Concave top and big bead ==lock the thumb in== for clean releases.

yes.title: True straight line
yes.t: Holds ==a gentle, predictable finish== on putts and drives.

yes.title: Tacky Pro blend
yes.t: ==Stays grippy==, even in rain, with a soft, rubbery feel.

no.title: Heat changes it
no.t: Pro plastic ==softens and feels sticky in summer==; gummier runs vary.

no.title: Divisive in the circle
no.t: Splits opinion: the deep, flexible build ==feels wrong to some putters==.

no.title: Shows heavy use
no.t: Lots of throws ==can warp it or wear the bead away==.

streamline-drift.tagline: An understable 7-speed fairway for shaping wooded lines. The catch: runs range from beefy to flippy.
streamline-drift.bottom: Great for newer and mid-level arms shaping tight lines. Skip it if every copy must match.

yes.title: Wooded-line control
yes.t: Stands up from hyzer and ==holds smooth lines through tight gaps==.

yes.title: Trustworthy out of the box
yes.t: Matches its rating new and ==beats a Leopard3 for accuracy==.

yes.title: Sidearm friendly
yes.t: Takes ==touchy forehands== cleanly off the rim.

no.title: Run-to-run swings
no.t: Splits opinion: copies range ==from overstable at 175 g to flipping off hyzer==.

no.title: Loosens up with use
no.t: Neutron copies ==gain turn as they wear== over a season.

discmania-sensei.tagline: A shallow, straight-flying throwing putter. The catch: stability varies a lot between copies.
discmania-sensei.bottom: A great throwing putter for beginners and intermediates. Skip it if every copy must match.

yes.title: Reliable throwing putter
yes.t: Tracks ==dead straight on approaches and short drives== with a soft finish.

yes.title: Low-profile build
yes.t: The shallow rim ==comes out of the hand cleanly== and suits smaller hands.

yes.title: Tacky plastics
yes.t: Baseline and Active Premium runs ==stay grippy, even in rain==.

no.title: Copy-to-copy swings
no.t: Splits opinion: copies range ==from too stable to flipping right away==.

no.title: Profile shifts by blend
no.t: Active Premium copies ==come out domey==, a shape some hands dislike.

no.title: Comfort varies
no.t: Some copies ==feel wrong in the hand==; mystery-box plastic left residue.

thought-space-athletics-construct.tagline: A glidey 10-speed for easy, straight distance. The catch: each blend flies very differently.
thought-space-athletics-construct.bottom: Best for intermediate and advanced arms chasing distance. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Repeatable lines
yes.t: ==Flies straight and holds its angle==, with no hyzer flip needed.

yes.title: Effortless distance
yes.t: Huge glide ==adds easy fairway carry==, out to about 400 ft.

yes.title: Sidearm friendly
yes.t: Flat forehands ==carry straight a long way==, Ethos especially.

no.title: Varies by blend
no.t: Ethos and Glow ==fly far beefier== than Aura, Ethereal or Aura Soft.

no.title: Flippier than stamped
no.t: Fresh Aura copies can ==turn right like a -2 and cook on hyzer==.

innova-wolf.tagline: A very understable DX mid for straight, turning lines. The catch: DX copies wear flippy fast.
innova-wolf.bottom: A classic first mid for beginners and anhyzer lines. Big arms should skip it.

yes.title: Anhyzer specialist
yes.t: Holds ==right-bending lines with no fade==, even at low speed.

yes.title: Learning disc
yes.t: Corrects weak hyzer releases and ==teaches newer players a straight shot==.

yes.title: Dead-straight option
yes.t: ==Flies with no curve== on easy forehands and long backhands.

no.title: Wears out fast
no.t: DX copies ==get too flippy after heavy use==, some in about 10 rounds.

no.title: Outgrown with power
no.t: Stronger arms ==turn it over and burn it out==.

discraft-wasp.tagline: A beaded, straight midrange with a dependable finish. The catch: it flies close to a Buzzz.
discraft-wasp.bottom: A reliable straight mid for beginners and intermediates. Skip it if you already bag a Buzzz.

yes.title: Rock-solid tracking
yes.t: Takes full power ==without flipping over==, then flies dead straight.

yes.title: Headwind helper
yes.t: A firmer finish than a Buzzz ==fights off wind==.

yes.title: Sidearm option
yes.t: Flat forehands ==go straight on holes under about 275 ft==.

no.title: Redundant slot
no.t: ==Flies close to a Buzzz==, so it can duplicate one in the bag.

no.title: Divisive rim detail
no.t: The bottom bead ==feels wrong to some hands==, worst on forehands.

latitude-64-compass.tagline: A neutral, glidey midrange that holds its angle. The catch: some runs lose their fade fast.
latitude-64-compass.bottom: A straight, versatile mid for beginners and intermediates. Skip it if you need a headwind mid.

yes.title: Shot-shape control
yes.t: ==Holds its release angle== and flies straight, from approaches to drives.

yes.title: Plenty of glide
yes.t: ==Carries a long way== and lands softly without flipping.

yes.title: One-disc versatility
yes.t: Covers ==most shots, from putts to full drives==.

no.title: Wears in quickly
no.t: Gold Ice and Retro copies ==lose their fade after some use==.

no.title: Weak in headwinds
no.t: Can ==flip up into the wind== and won't always fade out of anhyzer.

discraft-force.tagline: A 12-speed overstable driver for power and headwinds. The catch: stability swings by plastic and run.
discraft-force.bottom: Built for big arms needing wind and flex power. Beginners and 300 ft arms should skip it.

yes.title: Headwind weapon
yes.t: ==Resists turning over into stiff wind==, then hooks up with a skip.

yes.title: Long flex bomber
yes.t: Big anhyzer lines ==fight back to flat for huge carry==, near 450 ft.

yes.title: Sidearm power
yes.t: Takes ==aggressive forehands== without rolling over.

no.title: Blend and run swings
no.t: Z starts beefiest; ==ESP, Z Lite and Recycled plastic fly flippier==.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: ==Too much for 300 ft arms==, and it needs top power to fly far.

discraft-raptor.tagline: An overstable 9-speed for forehands and wind. The catch: it can turn over when light or thrown hard.
discraft-raptor.bottom: A forehand and wind fairway for intermediate and advanced arms. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Sidearm workhorse
yes.t: A go-to ==flick fairway driver==, easy to control off the fingers.

yes.title: Wind fighter
yes.t: Bores through headwinds and ==finishes with a hard, reliable skip==.

yes.title: Fairway line with a finish
yes.t: Holds ==straight for decent distance==, then fades predictably.

no.title: Milder than its peers
no.t: Can ==turn over when light or thrown hard==; less beefy than a Firebird.

no.title: Run-to-run swings
no.t: Z copies can ==meat-hook like a Firebird==; some puddle-tops show turn.

no.title: Divisive in hand
no.t: ESP can feel ==super hard==, and some throwers never click with it.

latitude-64-rive.tagline: A 13-speed overstable driver for wind and power. The catch: it beats in faster than its peers.
latitude-64-rive.bottom: A wind-fighting distance driver for strong arms. Beginners and slower arms should skip it.

yes.title: Wind anchor
yes.t: ==Resists turn into stiff breezes== and skips hard on landing.

yes.title: Big carry
yes.t: Pushes ==far before the fade kicks in==, past 350 ft on flat rips.

yes.title: Sidearm bomber
yes.t: ==Holds up to forehand torque== on long and tight flex lines.

no.title: Softens with wear
no.t: ==Beats in faster than a VIP-X Giant==, gaining early turn in a few rounds.

no.title: Varies by run
no.t: Royal and Orbit runs ==come out beefier==, while other copies feel mild.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: ==Needs a strong arm==; slower throwers only get it working on anhyzer.

mvp-control.tagline: A straight 10-speed with a dependable finish. The catch: it flies beefier than its numbers.
mvp-control.bottom: A reliable straight driver for intermediate and stronger arms. Arms near 300 ft should skip it.

yes.title: Dependable workhorse
yes.t: Holds ==dead straight with great carry==, then finishes left reliably.

yes.title: More stable sibling
yes.t: ==Resists the turnover a Trail shows==, pairing well with one in the bag.

yes.title: Sidearm ready
yes.t: Handles ==high-torque forehands== cleanly.

no.title: Beefier than rated
no.t: Fades ==earlier and harder than -0.5 turn suggests==, beyond a Trail.

no.title: Special editions vary
no.t: SE runs can ==fly off expectations and fight out early==.

mvp-octane.tagline: A 13-speed distance driver for big S-curves. The catch: each plastic flies very differently.
mvp-octane.bottom: Built for advanced arms chasing max distance. Beginners and slower arms should skip it.

yes.title: Big-arm bomber
yes.t: Pushes ==long S-curve distance==, past 400 ft for strong arms.

yes.title: Sidearm friendly
yes.t: Comfortable ==for big flicks and tight tunnels==.

yes.title: Lightweight turnover option
yes.t: Fission copies ==turn over and glide== for easy max distance.

no.title: Plastic lottery
no.t: Proton can ==meat-hook while Fission flips==; Neutron is hard to turn.

no.title: Less float than rivals
no.t: Neutron copies can ==fly flat and come up short== of a Destroyer.

dynamic-discs-verdict.tagline: An overstable midrange with a strong, dependable fade. The catch: it can flip a little into headwinds.
dynamic-discs-verdict.bottom: A trusty overstable mid for intermediate and advanced players. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Trusty finish
yes.t: Pushes straight, then ==hooks up with a strong, dependable fade==.

yes.title: Confident hand feel
yes.t: A flat top and blunt nose ==give a comfortable, sure grip==.

yes.title: Torque resistant
yes.t: Takes ==full power without high-speed turn==.

no.title: Wind can push it
no.t: Splits opinion: some copies ==flip a little into stiff headwinds==.

no.title: Blend changes it
no.t: Prime ==is a meathook==; Biofuzion and Lucid split on stability.

discraft-malita.tagline: A straight, slightly understable mid for tunnels. The catch: copies vary around a Buzzz SS.
discraft-malita.bottom: A forgiving straight mid for beginners and intermediates. Skip it if you already bag a Buzzz SS.

yes.title: Point-and-shoot accuracy
yes.t: Holds ==dead-straight tunnel lines== with a soft finish.

yes.title: Mild understability
yes.t: Flips up from hyzer and ==holds turn on a flat release==.

yes.title: Comfortable feel
yes.t: The slim, shallow rim ==sits nicely in smaller hands==.

no.title: Copy-to-copy swings
no.t: Splits opinion: copies ==range from flippier to stabler than a Buzzz SS==.

no.title: Familiar slot
no.t: Can ==fly just like a Buzzz or Buzzz SS== you may already bag.

discmania-tactic.tagline: An overstable approach putter for forehands and wind. The catch: Hard Exo copies can turn flippy fast.
discmania-tactic.bottom: A forehand and wind approach disc for intermediate and advanced players. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Sidearm approach weapon
yes.t: Shrugs off ==heavy forehand torque== without turning.

yes.title: Stops where it lands
yes.t: A sharp fade ==checks up without blowing past the basket==.

yes.title: Wind-ready upshots
yes.t: ==Stays reliable in strong headwinds== on short tee shots.

no.title: Baseline wears quickly
no.t: Hard Exo copies can ==fly straight or get flippy fast==.

no.title: Divisive against rivals
no.t: Splits opinion: it can ==feel less comfortable and fall short of a Zone==.

no.title: Limited reach
no.t: ==Lacks the distance of a mid== on longer upshots.

mvp-orbital.tagline: A very understable 11-speed for slow-arm distance. The catch: runs fly far more stable than -4.5.
mvp-orbital.bottom: A flippy distance driver for slower arms and roller shots. Big arms wanting a fade should skip it.

yes.title: Slow-arm distance
yes.t: Big turn and glide ==carry newer arms and turnover lines far==.

yes.title: Shot-shaping tool
yes.t: ==Swoops around big obstacles== and rolls a long way when asked.

yes.title: Extra reach off hyzer
yes.t: Steep releases ==fight the angle the whole way== down the fairway.

no.title: Run lottery
no.t: SE, glow and heavy copies ==fly far more stable than -4.5==.

no.title: Too flippy for some
no.t: Can ==turn over even from a knife hyzer== and roll off.

discraft-banger-gt.tagline: A grooved-top putter with a locked-in thumb feel. The catch: low glide makes it drop fast.
discraft-banger-gt.bottom: A confident putting and upshot disc for beginners and up. Skip it if you want a floaty putter.

yes.title: Thumb-groove feel
yes.t: The sunken track ==sets a natural placement== for clean, confident releases.

yes.title: Upshot specialist
yes.t: ==Hits and sticks== on approaches, with short rollaways.

yes.title: Confidence builder
yes.t: Became ==the putter that finally clicked== after long searches.

no.title: Low glide
no.t: ==Drops fast on putts==, so longer ones need extra push.

no.title: Divisive in the circle
no.t: Splits opinion: the track ==suits upshots more than putts== for some.
